name: editing-finished-drafts
description: Use when checking or editing a finished human-facing draft or batch for prose tells, unsupported claims, recipient fit, or repetitive shape before sharing it.
---

# Editing Finished Drafts

Return the supplied draft with its defects repaired and its useful content
intact. This pass owns verification and repair of an existing draft or batch.
Leave first drafting, code review, translation, exact substitutions, and posting
approved bytes to their owners.
It composes [writing-for-people](../writing-for-people/SKILL.md), which owns the
general register, evidence rules, and ordinary post-draft edit pass. Read that
skill and the references it calls for; use its named tells instead of maintaining
another checklist here. Specialized writers retain their content and format
contracts. Editing grants no authority to send or publish.

## Establish What Must Survive

Read the draft, supplied evidence, intended recipient and medium, and any
required wording or format. Recover available context before asking for it.
If the draft is missing, request it; do not invent a replacement. When a missing
recipient or purpose would change the edit materially, ask the specific question
and hold that decision.

Mark the author's purpose, supported claims, relevant first-person experience
and judgments, open questions, intended asks, and protected spans. Keep quoted
material, literal commands, retained text, and required structure intact. A
suspected error inside a protected span needs a separate note or a decision,
not an unannounced edit. A document's headings or deliberately parallel steps
can be part of its useful form.

## Inspect The Draft Against Its Inputs

Read once as its recipient: does the opening address what they came for, and
can they understand the point without the writer's internal task history?
Choose the register for this medium. Useful first-person evidence belongs in a
document too; document structure does not need to become a conversational reply.

Before editing, locate support outside the draft for each substantive clause.
Separate a sentence's premises from its conclusion: a qualified prediction
does not establish the mechanism it describes. Retain only the supported part
or identify the missing evidence.

Check each factual assertion against the supplied evidence, including numbers,
actors, causes, timing, confidence, and commitments. Distinguish what source
inspection establishes, what was observed in a run, and what remains a prediction
or judgment. Keep constructed test conditions attached when they limit the
claim. A confident sentence in the draft is not its own corroboration; missing
evidence also does not establish the opposite.

Run the general skill's edit pass to locate named tells. Judge each occurrence
in context: a phrase inside a required quotation, a useful label, or deliberate
parallel instructions is not disposable boilerplate. Mark concrete defects,
not a quota of changes.

For a batch, compare openings, closing moves, and length or structure across
pieces as well as within each one. Repair repetitive scaffolding from each
piece's own content. Keep order, separators, distinct recipients, and required
parallel formats; similar lengths alone do not justify padding or a new ask.

## Repair And Recheck

Edit the affected spans, preserving sound wording and supported substance.
Reorder only where the reader's understanding needs it. Correct contradicted
claims from the evidence; remove unsupported incidental assertions or qualify
them only when the qualification itself is supported. If a material assertion
cannot be checked, return the supported wording with the specific unresolved
fact identified. Do not silently remove the central question to make a draft
appear complete.

Compare the edited version with both the original and its evidence. Every
changed claim must retain its support, scope, and degree of certainty; every
removed substantive point needs a concrete reason. Check that useful evidence,
intentional form, asks, and protected spans survived. Reread the repaired text
as the recipient and, for a batch, compare the pieces again. Repeat for any
remaining defect introduced or missed by the edits. If nothing needs repair,
return the draft unchanged.

## Return The Edited Draft

Follow the requested output shape. Normally return the edited text, with only
material unresolved facts or protected-span problems noted separately when
needed. A request for final text alone does not make an unsupported central
claim publishable: state the specific gap if a supported final draft cannot
answer it. Include an edit rationale only when requested or needed to explain
such a gap. Completion means the draft meets its purpose without unsupported
claims, lost substance, or unresolved defects hidden by smoother prose.

---
name: writing-for-people
description: Use when drafting or editing prose for people, including publications, documentation, PR and Issue text, reports, chat messages, and review replies.
---

# Writing For People

## Scope

Own generic prose mechanics: grounding, register, organization, clarity,
evidence, and editing. The caller supplies personal voice. Surface owners
retain their content and format contracts: compose this guidance with the
applicable PR, Issue, or review writer, preserve retained text as its contract
requires, and leave publication and other actions to their authorized owners.

## Ground The Draft

Gather the source material, verified observations, decisions, open questions,
and the reader's purpose. Recover context from the available conversation and
artifacts before asking for discoverable facts. Distinguish what you know about
the audience from what you infer. Write a standalone artifact for a reader
arriving fresh; fold revision feedback into its substance.

## Choose The Register

Choose phrasing and structure for the medium, purpose, and audience. Lead the
piece and its sections with the subject the reader came for: the change,
finding, capability, question, or decision. Use first-person experience,
actions, judgments, and uncertainty where they help the reader assess that
subject. In publications and documents, these are usually supporting
statements; prefer subject-led openings. Let first person lead when the
writer's perspective is itself the subject, as in a personal account or a
reply about what the writer tried.

A publication explains its subject to readers beyond the exchange that
produced it. A conversation responds to what someone just said. A report,
proposal, guide, and reference document each need the organization their reader
will use. A public register can stay plain and approachable without turning
the artifact into a chat update or adopting an academic tone.

For chat, threaded comments, review replies, and status exchanges, read
[threaded-conversation.md](references/threaded-conversation.md). Apply those
exchange-specific rules only to that surface; a document requested in chat
still uses the document's register. Specialized writers own narrower
conventions, such as how a PR summarizes the change it applies.

## Build From Common Ground

Start from the context and language shared with the reader, giving enough
orientation for what follows. Explain a necessary unfamiliar term where it
appears; otherwise use plain words. Use technical precision where it changes
the reader's understanding or decision and everyday verbs elsewhere. When a
reader shows that an explanation did not land, recover the missing common
ground and explain more simply.

## Let Content Pick The Shape

Make the central point easy to find, then supply the motivation, evidence, and
detail needed to assess or act on it. Use headings, lists, tables, examples,
and conclusions when they serve the artifact's purpose. A short answer needs
little scaffolding; a procedure may need several steps, and a proposal may
need several decisions. Keep useful structure consistent across related
documents.

Spend emphasis in proportion to stakes. Give dense, important claims a
concrete instance, mention material caveats briefly, and keep each detail for
what it helps the reader understand or do. Describe verification in terms of
what it establishes, naming the machinery when readers need to rerun or audit
it. Credit a real strength when it helps explain the judgment.

## Bind Claims To Evidence

Distinguish behavior established from source from outcomes observed in a run.
A source-supported finding can be a plain declarative; an assertion that a
check passed needs the recorded observation. Separate the real system from
conditions constructed to test it. Identify an inference as an inference and
qualify only the uncertainty that remains, saying what causes it.

Read [evidence-in-prose.md](references/evidence-in-prose.md) when the draft
describes system behavior, reports an outcome, makes a commitment, or states
what someone did. Keep claims within the evidence and decisions supplied or
verified for the task.

## Edit Before Delivery

Run [edit-pass.md](references/edit-pass.md) on the finished draft. Check its
register against the intended surface, its structure against the reader's
purpose, and every factual claim against the evidence after rewriting. For
text going to a reviewer, a shared channel, or a customer, make a second pass
for distracting mannerisms and factual drift.

# Edit Pass

Run this pass over the finished draft before delivery. Judge edits against the
medium and purpose selected in the main skill, including useful structure and
the caller's personal voice.

## 1. Judge Each Dash

Scan for em dashes and for " - " used as a dash, then judge each one by
its usage. A parenthetical dash (an inserted phrase read inline) is
written unspaced: `the cache—once wired up—drops the call`. A bespoke,
non-parenthetical usage may be spaced; keep it only when the spacing is
doing work a reader would miss. Where a dash is not the best structure,
use a colon, parentheses, a semicolon, or a new sentence. Judge fit, not
count.

Check the rest of the typography while here. An en dash joins numeric
ranges (3–5) and compound modifiers built on an open compound. Inline
lists take the Oxford comma. Punctuation respects the unity of a quoted
phrase rather than intruding into it: the flag is `--force-with-lease`,
not `--force-with-lease,`.

## 2. Reread The Last Sentence

Reread the ending. Keep a conclusion or recap when the artifact needs one;
remove a flourish or repetition that adds nothing for its reader. In a reply,
end on the last substantive point. Watch for:

- A moral drawn from the point just made ("That's where the real cost
  hides.").
- A restatement dressed as a conclusion ("So the guard does its job.").
- An unrelated ask attached as an afterthought to a threaded comment.

## 3. Strike On Sight

Delete or rewrite these wherever they appear:

- "worth noting", "worth also", "It's important to", "credit where due",
  "That said".
- Arrow chains (`A → B → C`) standing in for an explanation the reader needs.
- Empty topic labels or process lead-ins that delay the subject. Preserve
  descriptive headings and useful first-person evidence or judgment.
- Unexplained jargon or coinages. Define a necessary term where it stands or
  replace it with plain words.
- Apologetic framing, hedge stacks, throat-clearing, sycophancy, and
  explanations the source already provides.

## 4. Vary Across A Batch

When sending several comments or replies together, compare them for repeated
openings, closings, or cadence that obscure their individual substance. Vary
those as needed. Keep consistent structures when they help readers navigate
or compare related documents and records.

## 5. Reread As The Recipient

Read the piece as its intended reader, in the place they will encounter it.
Replace mechanical phrasing, needless precision, and displays of effort with
clear prose suited to that medium. Keep the shortest phrasing that preserves
meaning and reads naturally; conversational speech is one register among
several.

## 6. Recheck Every Fact

Fluent rewriting is where facts drift: "should fail" becomes "fails", a
range becomes a point, a question becomes a commitment. Check each fact
against the brief after every rewrite, not only when first written. Full
rules: [evidence-in-prose.md](evidence-in-prose.md).

# Evidence In Prose

## Gather The Facts First

Most invented details come from a thin brief. Before drafting, gather:

- What was run, on what, and what it returned.
- What was decided, by whom, and what is still open.
- What the reader asked, in their words.
- What the reader already knows, so the draft neither repeats it nor
  assumes more.

Say what you did not check, and let the reader look up what the draft
does not carry. Before asking for a fact, check the transcript and the
artifacts you already have; ask only for what they cannot tell you.

## Guards

### Distinguish Source Findings From Observed Outcomes

State behavior established by inspected source as such: "`parse_limit` rejects
negative values" can follow from its guard without a runtime experiment.
Keep the claim within what that source establishes. A report that a test or
command passed, a deployment completed, or a live system behaved a certain way
needs a recorded run and result. Attach the observation where it matters:
"`make check` exits 1 on the fixture branch". Use a condition or modal for an
unverified prediction, such as "this should fail once the cache is wired up".

### Never Commit To An Undecided Position

Do not commit yourself, or the people you write for, to a position,
threshold, offer, deadline, or concession that is not in the brief.
Offer options, ask the question, or name the decision as open and say
who holds it.

### Write The Observation, Not The Story

Report the observation accurately: "the config record hasn't changed since
June 2" does not by itself establish that the update silently failed. Include
an inference when it helps, identifying it as a judgment and giving its basis
and remaining uncertainty.

### Leave Out Social Facts You Do Not Have

Who asked, what happened, when, and why someone acted are facts like any
other. When one is not in evidence, ask or leave it out. Do not supply a
plausible actor or motive to make a sentence flow.

### Separate The System From The Setup

When reporting a check you ran, separate what the real system does from
conditions you constructed to run it. "The endpoint returns 429 after
the tenth request in a minute" and "I hit it with a loop of twelve
requests against a local build" are different facts; give the reader
both when the second changes how far the first can be trusted.

## Qualify Only Real Uncertainty

State a confident finding as a plain declarative. Qualify a claim only
when it is genuinely uncertain, and say what makes it so ("my best
guess from the current API shape; I couldn't find a direct caller").
When every claim carries a hedge, the reader cannot tell which one needs
it.
candidate_bundle.skills/writing-for-people/references/thr:
# Threaded Conversation

Use this guidance for chat messages, threaded comments, review replies, and
status exchanges. Apply the main skill's medium and structure rules to any
standalone artifact delivered within that exchange.

## Respond To The Live Point

Open by answering what the person asked or engaging what they just said or
did. When initiating, lead with what the reader most needs. Match their
register and conversational energy while staying professional, and acknowledge
social intent when it matters. Put a finding directly before its explanation;
a concrete mechanism or code symbol helps when the reader shares that context.
For questions about impact or progress, lead with the reader-relevant outcome
and its material limits, then explain the cause or the work behind it.

Let each next point answer a likely follow-up, doubt, or challenge. Keep replies
focused on the exchange, and end on the last substantive point. First-person
observations and judgments fit when they answer the question or identify who
holds the view.

## Keep The Exchange Actionable

Give each threaded comment one coherent point and, when action is needed, one
clear ask. Split unrelated asks into separate comments. An answer,
acknowledgment, or completed-action report may need no ask. A multi-part
question or a broader status exchange may need several connected answers;
organize them for the person responding.

In a review reply, agreement can be brief: say what follows without repeating
the comment or explaining why the suggestion is sensible. Include a correction
or tradeoff when the reviewer needs it. Review-specific severity and ask forms
belong to the review writer's policy.

## Keep The Reply Proportionate

Use connected paragraphs for a substantial reply; use a list or collapsed
detail when it makes the exchange easier to follow. Avoid ceremonial topic
labels and an inventory of the work merely to show effort. Preserve enough
context for someone joining the thread to understand the point.

When a work report stops at an authorization or scope boundary, say so plainly
and distinguish it from a technical blocker. State what remains and the next
decision or action. When sending a batch of comments, let each one's substance
shape its opening and cadence; keep a shared format where it helps comparison.

# Context
The section is for maintainers reading the export guide. The supplied code inspection establishes that `retry_limit` defaults to 3 and counts retries after the first attempt. A local test used a stub that failed every request; its log contains one first attempt and three retries. Production was not observed. Nobody supplied a rollout date or customer-loss measurements.

# Draft
## Retry limits
It's worth noting that `retry_limit` defaults to 3. This isn't about waiting longer—it's about reliable exports. The worker makes at most three total attempts. I tested the local worker with a stub that failed every request and saw three retries after the first attempt. Production now recovers without losing any exports. That said, the change goes live for all customers on Friday.

Set `retry_limit` to choose how many retries follow the first attempt.

method.model_selection: Inherited model and reasoning settings; no override or independent provider attestation.
method.delivery: Each fresh agent received one packet path, read it locally, and was instructed to use only the packet and return the requested text.
method.restrictions: One initial read allowed; no subsequent tools requested. Instructional restrictions, not enforced tool denial or filesystem isolation.
method.ambient_limit: Provider/system instructions, installed skill metadata, and harness ambient guidance remain available. Task-history exclusion does not establish an isolated baseline.
method.telemetry_limit: No independently exported provider trace, normalized context, token accounting, or completion timing.
method.response_capture: Native final messages transcribed verbatim with one trailing newline.
method.baseline: No current comparative baseline is claimed. Earlier preparation outputs remain historical evidence for their frozen dependency bundle.
method.claim: Qualitative application of explicitly supplied instructions on six synthetic cases; no discovery, release, installation, or runtime-enforcement qualification.
